title: Magnon Super-Bloch Oscillations and Switchable Transport in Driven Magnonic Crystals
authors: Xiang Liu, Xi-guang Wang, Zhi-xiong Li, Xiufeng Han, Guang-hua Guo
abstract: Super-Bloch oscillations (SBOs) offer a powerful route to control wave packet propagation in driven lattices, yet their realization in magnonic systems has remained elusive. Here, we predict SBOs of magnon wave packets in periodic magnonic crystals driven by static and ac gradients of magnetic anisotropy field. A static gradient alone induces magnon Bloch oscillation (BO) with a constant carrier frequency. Remarkably, adding a near-resonant MHz-scale ac driving gives rise to a slow large-amplitude envelope oscillation, the hallmark of SBO. At exact resonance, the ac driving enables phase-controlled directional transport with a carrier-frequency shift up to GHz scale. Consequently, the same structure can be switched among three distinct regimes: conventional BO, SBO, and directed transport. Analytical expressions for the oscillation amplitudes, superperiod, drift velocity, and frequency evolution are validated by micromagnetic simulations. Extending to antiferromagnet magnonic crystals, we further demonstrate that these effects drive opposite motions of two oppositely polarized magnon modes in THz range. Our work establishes magnon SBOs as a versatile platform, opening a new avenue for reconfigurable magnonic devices.
summary: This work predicts and analyzes Super-Bloch Oscillations in magnonic crystals driven by patterned magnetic fields. By applying a near-resonant AC drive, the system can be switched between standard Bloch Oscillation, SBO, and highly directional transport. This establishes magnonics as a versatile platform for reconfigurable wave manipulation in condensed matter devices.
main_problem: The study aims to demonstrate and analyze Super-Bloch Oscillations (SBOs) and the resulting switchable transport regimes in magnonic crystals.
main_result: The system can be switched between conventional Bloch Oscillation (BO), SBO, and highly directional transport by tuning the frequency and phase of an applied AC magnetic gradient field.
method: The analysis uses a linearized model derived from the LLG equation, mapping the dynamics onto a Schrödinger equation to derive analytical expressions for oscillation amplitudes and drift velocity.
model_or_system: The physical system is a magnonic crystal (e.g., YIG film) where magnon wave packets propagate under the influence of static and AC gradients of the magnetic anisotropy field.
key_observables: Oscillation amplitudes ($A_0, A_1$), superperiod ($T_{	ext{super}}$), drift velocity ($v_m$), and time-dependent carrier frequency evolution.
important_parameters: The driving fields include static and near-resonant AC gradients; key parameters involve the detuning ($\delta$) and the phase ($\phi$) of the AC drive.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on linearizing the magnon dynamics and projecting the motion onto the lowest magnon band.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic of the crystal, the dependence of motion/spectra on gradient strengths and detuning, and crucially, how the initial phase ($\phi$) controls the direction of magnon transport.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the BO mechanism with a static gradient, then introducing the AC drive to generate SBOs, and finally analyzing the resonant regime where phase control enables directional transport, extending the concept to AFM crystals.
why_interesting: The concept of SBOs and phase-controlled transport in magnonics provides an analogy to wave packet control in quantum systems, offering a platform for reconfigurable devices analogous to quantum signal routing.
